EE.Settings.HideDmTokens.Name: Hide DM-dropped tokens from players
EE.Settings.HideDmTokens.Hint: When you (the GM) drop a token onto a scene, make it invisible to players while still letting them target and interact with it. Toggle any single token from its HUD with the eye icon.
Make hidden tokens untouchable for players

Players can't hover, click, select, drag or box-select a token that's hidden from them, and can't nudge one with the arrow keys — as far as they can tell it isn't on the board at all. Targeting is unaffected, and so is anything that measures distance between tokens. Players still choose which of their own tokens is active from the Tokens on Scene bar.
EE.Settings.DisableDragAnimation.Name: Disable token drag animation
EE.Settings.DisableDragAnimation.Hint: Dragging and dropping a token moves it instantly instead of gliding it to the destination at Foundry's fixed animation speed. Applies to everyone at the table, and only to drag-and-drop — keyboard movement still animates.
EE.Settings.TokenBar.Name: Show players a "Tokens on Scene" bar
EE.Settings.TokenBar.Hint: Give each player a small floating list of the tokens they own on the current scene, so they can choose which one they're driving without hunting for it on the canvas — necessary when tokens are hidden from players. Players can drag the bar wherever they like; the GM never sees it.
EE.Settings.TokenBarLockSelection.Name: Never leave a player with nothing selected
EE.Settings.TokenBarLockSelection.Hint: If a player deselects their last token — by clicking empty ground, pressing Escape, or switching tools — put it straight back. Without this, their HUD falls back to whichever character it finds first, which may not be theirs.
EE.TokenBar.Title: Tokens on Scene
EE.TokenBar.SurveyTooltip: See what's on this scene and how far away it is
EE.TokenBar.SelectRefused: That token can't be selected right now. Switch back to the Select tool and try again.
EE.Settings.HotbarPageSwap.Name: Swap hotbar page on token selection
EE.Settings.HotbarPageSwap.Hint: Selecting a token switches the hotbar to the page assigned to that token's character. Nothing else in this window has any effect until this is on.
EE.Settings.RefreshRaisedPortraits.Name: Refresh raised portraits on artwork change
EE.Settings.RefreshRaisedPortraits.Hint: When a character's portrait image changes while Ginzzzu's Portraits is showing it, update the raised portrait to match instead of leaving the old artwork on screen. Portraits with a custom image or an active emotion are left alone.
EE.Settings.RollRequestClose.Name: Close the cinematic roll prompt after rolling
EE.Settings.RollRequestClose.Hint: When you request a roll in Cinematic Mode, close the player's prompt window once they've rolled instead of leaving it on screen over the result. Needs Daggerheart: Quick Actions.
EE.Settings.RollRequestOptions.Name: Let players choose advantage and Experiences on a roll request
EE.Settings.RollRequestOptions.Hint: Put Advantage/Disadvantage buttons and the character's Experiences (1 Hope each) on the roll request itself — on the cinematic prompt and on the whispered chat card — and roll it as the character the player is driving. Advantage or disadvantage you set in the request is shown but locked. Without this, a requested roll can't apply an Experience at all, and rolls with no character behind it for any player who has no assigned actor. Needs Daggerheart: Quick Actions.
EE.RollRequest.LockedByGm: Set by the GM for this roll.
EE.Settings.GeneralFeaturesMenu.Name: General Features
EE.Settings.GeneralFeaturesMenu.Label: Configure
EE.Settings.GeneralFeaturesMenu.Hint: Token visibility and selection, drag movement, and keeping raised portraits in step with character artwork.
EE.Settings.HotbarPagesMenu.Name: Per-Token Hotbars
EE.Settings.HotbarPagesMenu.Label: Configure Assignments
EE.Settings.HotbarPagesMenu.Hint: Choose which hotbar page each character switches to, and which page to fall back to for everything else.
EE.HotbarPages.Title: Per-Token Hotbars
EE.HotbarPages.Notes: Assign a character to a hotbar page and the bar switches to that page whenever one of its tokens is selected.
EE.HotbarPages.DefaultHint: Shown when an unassigned token is selected, or when nothing is selected at all.
EE.HotbarPages.ApplyToPlayersHint: Off by default: players keep their own macros on their own pages, so only your hotbar follows the selection.
EE.HotbarPages.NoActors: This world has no actors to assign.
EE.Settings.DaggerheartAutomationMenu.Hi: Apply Daggerheart rules the table would otherwise have to remember, and hook up Daggerheart-specific modules such as The Void.
EE.Settings.ReachMeleeAsVeryClose.Name: Reach
EE.Settings.ReachMeleeAsVeryClose.Hint: Give any character holding a feature called "Reach" — the Giant ancestry's — the range it describes: every weapon, ability, spell, or other feature of theirs with a Melee range works as though it were Very Close. Sheets, tooltips and target pickers all read the longer range. Nothing is saved to the cards themselves, so removing the feature (or this option) puts Melee straight back.
EE.Settings.FearlessFearToHope.Name: Fearless
EE.Settings.FearlessFearToHope.Hint: Let a character holding the Infernis "Fearless" feature use it: whenever they roll with Fear, offer to mark 2 Stress and turn it into a roll with Hope. Taking the offer converts the roll before anything reacts to the Fear — the GM gains no Fear, Fear countdowns don't advance, and other features that trigger on a Fear roll never fire. Declining, or letting the prompt time out, leaves the roll exactly as it landed.
EE.Settings.BloodMaledictReroll.Name: Blood Maledict
EE.Settings.BloodMaledictReroll.Hint: Let a character holding the Void's "Blood Maledict" feature use it: whenever an adversary within Close range succeeds on an attack roll, offer to spend 3 Hope and make it reroll with disadvantage. The GM's client pauses the attack and puts the question on the character's owner's screen; taking it replaces the roll before the chat card is posted, so the original hit never becomes damage. Needs both actors on the scene — a range that can't be measured raises no prompt.
EE.Settings.CrimsonRiteEnchant.Name: Crimson Rite
EE.Settings.CrimsonRiteEnchant.Hint: Make the Void's "Crimson Rite" feature do what it says. Marking the Hit Point asks which active weapon to enchant (silently, if only one is equipped) and grants that weapon a tier-scaled bonus — 1d4 rising to 4d4 — which the system expires at the character's next rest, short or long. Using the feature again moves the rite rather than stacking it. The enchanted weapon's damage also counts as magic, which is the part the Void's own tier effects never managed on an ordinary physical weapon.
EE.Settings.BloodSpikeSpendHope.Name: Blood Spike
EE.Settings.BloodSpikeSpendHope.Hint: Resolve the Void's "Blood Spike" card in one press. Either of its attack actions now rolls the die the rule calls for — a d10 once the caster has 3 or more Hit Points marked, a d8 below that — so the d8 and d10 buttons stop being a choice you can get wrong, in either direction. On a hit, the caster is asked whether to spend the Hope: taking it rolls the damage as usual, declining rolls none, and the target marks its Stress either way (that part is already the card's own damage part, applied only to targets that were hit). A miss asks nothing. The card's separate "Spend Hope" action is left alone, as the manual route for a cast resolved without a target.
EE.Settings.HoldThemOffExtraTargets.Name: Hold Them Off
EE.Settings.HoldThemOffExtraTargets.Hint: Let a Ranger holding "Hold Them Off" use it: after a successful attack with a weapon, offer to spend 3 Hope and pick up to two more adversaries within the attack's range. Whoever is picked is added to the attack itself before the chat card is posted, so the one roll and the one damage roll resolve against all of them at once — hit or miss decided per adversary against their own Difficulty, exactly as if they had been targeted before the swing. The picker lists only adversaries the player can see and whose distance can be measured; it never shows anyone's Difficulty. Needs the attacker on the scene — a range that can't be measured raises no prompt, and neither does an unarmed strike or a Ranger below 3 Hope.
EE.Settings.ISeeItComingEvasion.Name: I See It Coming
EE.Settings.ISeeItComingEvasion.Hint: Let a character holding the Bone domain's "I See It Coming" card use it: whenever an attack made from beyond Melee range lands on them, offer to mark a Stress, roll a d4 and add it to their Evasion against that attack. The attacker's client pauses the roll and puts the question on the character's owner's screen; taking it can turn the hit into a miss before the chat card is posted, so the hit never becomes damage. The d4 is posted to chat, whispered as far as the attack itself. Needs both actors on the scene — a range that can't be measured raises no prompt, and neither does an attack rolled against a fixed difficulty rather than Evasion.
EE.Settings.VoidHybridFormPortrait.Name: Sync portrait to Hybrid Form
EE.Settings.VoidHybridFormPortrait.Hint: When The Void puts an Order of the Lycan character into Hybrid Form, change the character sheet portrait to match the transformed token art, and change it back when the form is dropped.
EE.Settings.VoidHybridFormPrototype.Name: Also transform the prototype token
EE.Settings.VoidHybridFormPrototype.Hint: Additionally rewrite the character's prototype token, so a token dragged onto a scene mid-transformation arrives in Hybrid Form. Off by default: unlike the portrait, this changes saved character data.
EE.Settings.VoidHybridFormStressRevert.N: End Hybrid Form when Stress is full
EE.Settings.VoidHybridFormStressRevert.H: When an Order of the Lycan character's Stress reaches its maximum while transformed, automatically revert them to human form, the same way clicking the wolf button would. Complements The Void's own rule that gaining Hope while transformed also marks Stress, which it never reverts the form for.

EE.Settings.DaggerheartUtilitiesMenu.Hin: Table rules for Daggerheart play, such as capping how many decks are in play at once.
EE.Settings.DeckLimitEnabled.Name: Limit the number of decks
EE.Settings.DeckLimitEnabled.Hint: Cap how many decks can be in play at once. Off by default — nothing is limited until you turn this on.
EE.Settings.DeckLimitCount.Name: Number of decks
EE.Settings.DeckLimitCount.Hint: How many decks the limit above allows. Minimum 1.
EE.Settings.DeckLimitPlayersOnly.Name: Only limit player characters
EE.Settings.DeckLimitPlayersOnly.Hint: Count and restrict only characters assigned to (or owned by) a player. Your own character sheets — pregens, test characters, retired PCs — stay out of the pool entirely: they don't use up copies, and they aren't blocked from taking any. Off by default, where every character in the world draws from the decks.
EE.Utilities.Title: Daggerheart Utilities
EE.Utilities.DeckContentsHint: Copies of each card a single deck contains, multiplied by the number of decks above to get the pool. The defaults match a printed Daggerheart deck — change them if your table proxies or homebrews extra cards. Zero means a deck holds none of that card type.
EE.DeckLimit.OnHoldBy: On hold: {holders} — picked but not yet confirmed.
EE.DeckLimit.HeldByNobody: Nobody is holding it — the deck simply doesn't contain one.
EE.DeckLimit.BlockedBody: All {pool} copies of {name} are already in play, so there isn't one left to take.
EE.DeckLimit.BlockedAsk: If you need it anyway, ask your GM — they can add it for you.
EE.DeckLimit.ExceedBody: All {pool} copies of {name} are already in play. Adding this one puts more copies on the table than the decks hold.
EE.DeckLimit.ExceedHint: You're the GM, so this is allowed — this is only a check that you meant it.
EE.DeckLimit.TooltipNone: Deck limit — the deck holds none of these
EE.DeckLimit.TooltipOnHold: On hold by {holders} — picked in an open character creation or level-up, but not confirmed yet
EE.Settings.SessionLogMenu.Name: Session Log
EE.Settings.SessionLogMenu.Label: Configure Log
EE.Settings.SessionLogMenu.Hint: Keep a running log of what happens during the session, for combining with the Discord voice transcript afterward to draft session notes.
EE.Settings.SessionLogEnabled.Name: Enable Session Log
EE.Settings.SessionLogEnabled.Hint: Start recording notable session events to the log. Off by default.
EE.Settings.SessionLogRolls.Name: Log dice rolls
EE.Settings.SessionLogRolls.Hint: Record each Duality/reaction roll's result — the total and whether it came up Hope, Fear, or a Critical Success.
EE.Settings.SessionLogResources.Name: Log resource changes
EE.Settings.SessionLogResources.Hint: Record Hit Point, Stress, Armor, and Hope changes as they happen.
EE.Settings.SessionLogStatus.Name: Log status changes
EE.Settings.SessionLogStatus.Hint: Record conditions and other effects gained or lost, and when a character goes down.
EE.Settings.SessionLogCombat.Name: Log combat
EE.Settings.SessionLogCombat.Hint: Record when combat begins and ends.
EE.Settings.SessionLogScenes.Name: Log scene changes
EE.Settings.SessionLogScenes.Hint: Record when you activate a different scene.
EE.Settings.SessionLogFlags.Name: Log GM flags
EE.Settings.SessionLogFlags.Hint: Record moments you flag manually from the chat log button.
EE.SessionLog.Title: Session Log
EE.SessionLog.ExportHint: Export the most recent session's entries to a page in the "Session Logs" journal, in the "Utility Suite" folder. Completed sessions are also exported automatically the next time something is logged after a 12-hour gap.
EE.SessionLog.ExportEmpty: There's nothing in the Session Log to export yet.
EE.SessionLog.Exported: Session exported to the "Session Logs" journal.
EE.SessionLog.FlagButton: Flag this moment for the session log
